subject: POC intake: prompt/log bundle and success criteria (NovaLedger)
messages:
From: Sam Doe <sam.doe@novaledger.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@novaledger.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + POC scope follow-up

Tessa — thanks for the call today. Quick recap from our side and some clarification requests so we can mobilize the team: 

- Goal: 2-week POC to validate Redwood inference on our customer support routing and canned-response suggestions. Primary success metric is actionable suggestion rate and low hallucination (false/confident incorrect suggestions).
- Data we can provide: 25k de-identified support prompts (CSV), and sample conversation logs (S3). We need guidance on the schema and any anonymization checklist.
- Security: we will need a short MSA addendum for data handling; legal looped in.

Can you send the exact prompt/log format you need, plus an S3 upload guide and owner list? Also propose success criteria thresholds we can agree on for the trial.

—Sam

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Doe <sam.doe@novaledger.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@novaledger.com>, Legal Team <legal@novaledger.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC intake: prompt/log bundle and success criteria (NovaLedger)

Sam — great to connect. See below a proposed intake checklist and evaluation plan. I attached the templates referenced (poc-success-criteria-template.xlsx, sample_prompts_schema.md, s3-upload-instructions.txt). High-level: 2-week trial, Redwood-hosted, dedicated test model instance.

Intake checklist (what we need from NovaLedger):
- Prompt bundle: CSV with columns [prompt_id, user_text, channel, timestamp, metadata_tags]. Anonymize PII per our sample_prompts_schema.md.
- Conversation logs: gzipped JSONL with one event per line; if you cannot export JSONL, a CSV of utterances is fine.
- Positive/negative labels (optional): if you have 1–2k examples of “accepted” vs “rejected” suggestions, include as label column named "outcome".
- Target success metrics (workshop to finalize): suggestion acceptance >= 22%, hallucination rate <= 2% (definition: returned entity/assertion not verifiable in transcript), median generation latency < 220ms.
- Ownership: NovaLedger data owner: Priya Mehta. Redwood POC lead: Tessa Morgan. Infra escalation: Sean Gallagher.
- Timeline: data handoff by Jan 18; onboarding + dry run Jan 19–20; evaluation window Jan 22–Feb 2; final readout Feb 5.

Next steps:
1) Priya — confirm dataset availability and whether labels exist.
2) Legal — can you review the MSA/data addendum I attached and confirm any changes?
3) NovaLedger — please upload a 2k sample subset to the S3 path in s3-upload-instructions.txt so we can validate parsing.

I included specific acceptance thresholds above but open to adjusting during our final success criteria session. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync early next week to finalize.

Best,
Tessa
POC Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@novaledger.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Doe <sam.doe@novaledger.com>, Legal Team <legal@novaledger.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC intake: prompt/log bundle and success criteria (NovaLedger)

Tessa — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers: 
- We can deliver the prompt CSV and JSONL logs. We also have ~1.5k labeled accept/reject examples; we'll include them.
- Security: legal will review the addendum; Sam your infra team will provision a short-term project bucket.
- Timeline: we will aim to place the sample subset in the S3 path by EOD Jan 18. Full bundle by Jan 19 close of business.

Question for Redwood: for the labels, do you prefer a separate labels file or a column in the primary CSV? Also, what naming convention should we use for prompt_ids to avoid collisions?

—Priya

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@novaledger.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Sam Doe <sam.doe@novaledger.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC intake: prompt/log bundle and success criteria (NovaLedger)

Priya — short answers: 
- Labels: either works; we typically prefer a labels column named "outcome" in the primary CSV to keep mappings explicit, but a separate CSV keyed by prompt_id is fine if you already have that layout.
- prompt_id convention: NL-YYYYMMDD-XXXX (e.g., NL-20280118-0001). Please avoid spaces; IDs should be unique within the bundle.
- Schema: follow sample_prompts_schema.md — small variations are okay but call them out in a README in the bundle root.

Also adding parsing notes: if you include HTML in user_text, flag it in metadata_tags as "html:true". For timestamps, ISO-8601 preferred (UTC offset ok).

I'll triage the onboarding checklist once the sample is uploaded and ping Sean if infra changes required.

Thanks — Lauren

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@novaledger.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Doe <sam.doe@novaledger.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jan 2028 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC intake: prompt/log bundle and success criteria (NovaLedger)

Priya — quick infra notes after I reviewed your bucket policy. Two asks before we consume data:

1) Please provide the sample subset at s3://redwood-nl-poc/samples/2028-01-18/ with object ACLs restricted to the project role. I attached s3-upload-instructions.txt with exact presigned policy we accept.
2) For anonymization: remove or hash email addresses and payment identifiers; if you must include hashed IDs, use SHA-256 and include a note in README.

Once sample is uploaded I will run an ingestion dry-run (non-destructive) and report parsing errors within 24 hours. If all good, we will provision a short-lived dedicated instance and begin the dry run Jan 19.

Ping me when upload is complete and include the object manifest URL.

—Sean
